May 3, 2026 Checkout supports advance collection when the final charge amount or date is decided later, with a Customer association for later reuse. The manual hosted and embedded examples use mode=setup and include sepa_debit with card, using success_url hosted or return_url and ui_mode=embedded_page embedded (old 20–83). The examples do not make card required. The same passage calls a later SEPA payment delayed and gives a typically five-business-day arrival estimate, separate from setup. This timing is dated, not a guaranteed deadline and not a replacement for the concept's different T+6 standard settlement statement (concept 19–27).

May's generic Accounts v2 preface recommends customer-configured Accounts for most cases and describes Connect GA versus public preview for other users with a preview version if enrolled (old 8–14); the actual three branches shown create/retrieve a Customers API Customer and pass customer, not a customer_account example (old 28–42,481–512,1061–1092). This matters to interpretation of source line 19. The old Elements section recommends prebuilt Checkout when using Stripe's Creditor ID (old 456–463).

Old web Elements 497–567 and 625–723 describe a server-created SetupIntent for sepa_debit with a Customer, a carefully handled client secret, a mounted Payment Element collecting name/email/IBAN and displaying/handling mandate acceptance, and stripe.confirmSetup. Success is SetupIntent status succeeded and attaches the PaymentMethod to the supplied Customer, handling a returned error on failure. The paired old and new documents do not give the source's web-confirmation modal claim or its asserted SetupIntent webhook list (source 24–25). Stripe.js confirmSepaDebitSetup link only appears in an old React Native test paragraph (1204–1210), distinct from the actual React Native client confirmation example (1161–1202).

Old React Native 981–1092,1094–1130 and 1161–1202 uses server SetupIntent creation, app collection of IBAN and mandate terms for implicit acceptance, then confirmSetupIntent with SepaDebit and the client secret. The old guide requires billingDetails addressCountry and addressLine1 for the listed IBAN country codes at line 1167. Native iOS and Android are platform dependencies within React Native (1004–1024), not separate variants in either capture, contrary to summary lines 13 and 38 and concept line 115.

Old 85–338,724–977 and 1204–1457 use 19-country test IBAN/PaymentMethod tokens. Do not treat these as SetupIntent transitions, geographic product eligibility, or payment success. The neighboring accept-payment source link at summary 34 is useful navigation, but identity with all its raw values is outside this review.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-sepa-debit-set-up-payment-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-sepa-set-up-payment-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-sepa-set-up-payment.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sepa-debit/set-up-payment`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sepa-debit/set-up-payment establishes a selector for saving SEPA Direct Debit details and lists Checkout, Elements and Mobile React Native (new raw lines 5-16). May 3, 2026 describes advance collection through Checkout setup mode for an attached Customer, with hosted success_url and embedded return_url, and notes delayed notification and typical five-business-day arrival for a later payment (old raw lines 16-83). The merchant server creates a SEPA SetupIntent for a Customer and hands the client its secret. The mounted web Payment Element collects details and handles mandate acceptance, and confirmSetup establishes setup status and attachment after success (old raw lines 481-567 and 625-723). React Native collects IBAN and communicates mandate terms, then uses confirmSetupIntent and has specified billing address fields for the listed IBAN countries (old raw lines 1061-1202). Later-charge test cases distinguish PaymentIntent processing/success/failure and dispute from successful setup (old raw lines 1204-1223). source-stripe-sepa-set-up-payment.md correctly captures the Checkout and SetupIntent distinction and optional reference prefix but wrongly lists independent native iOS/Android paths, conflates web confirmation UI/methods, and assigns webhook evidence absent from these captures. November contributes navigation only.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sepa-debit/set-up-payment, the November 7, 2026 full-to-index change is presentational and navigation-only. The index points to the same Checkout, Elements and React Native variants marked in the May 3, 2026 guide (new raw lines 9-16, old raw lines 16-18, 456-458, and 981-983). No product removal, addition or capability change is established. Preserve the May hosted/embedded setup, explicit Customer examples separately from Accounts v2 preview guidance, mandate collection and setup-versus-later-debit states, React Native country-specific billing-address condition, and optional prefix validation including its required first character (old raw lines 8-14, 28-83, 1094-1202 and 1459-1474). The baseline source-stripe-sepa-set-up-payment.md needs the platform and confirmation corrections, and the dated React Native test prose mismatch (old raw lines 1204-1210) should remain distinct from the demonstrated SDK call (old raw lines 1161-1202). May's Checkout setup discussion gives a typical five-business-day arrival estimate for a later SEPA debit (old raw lines 20-27), while the Stripe SEPA Direct Debit concept records standard T+6 payment success and funds availability (concept lines 19–27). Both are later-payment timing descriptions. Neither changes setup status or establishes a guaranteed account-specific deadline. Preserve the historical raw, root-to-Stripe index route, Stripe SEPA Direct Debit concept link and reciprocal source route, and separate accept-payment and Connect navigation. The linked child variants carry no fresh behavior evidence here.
